core_definitions.term: A participant who controls one or more characters.
A persona used by a player in the game world.
A character controlled by a player.
Another term for a player character.
The referee who prepares adventures, adjudicates rules, narrates the world, and controls NPCs and monsters.
A character controlled by the Judge.
A collective term for PCs, NPCs, and monsters.
Numerical measures of a character's talents and aptitudes.
A character's profession or training type; determines development and abilities.
A measure of a character's advancement and power within a class.
Generally a 0th level character.
Advancement currency earned partly from defeated monsters and mostly from treasure returned to civilization.
A relative measure of a monster's challenge.
A relative measure of a spell's power; does not directly correspond to class level.
A measure of survivability. At 0 or fewer hp, a being is incapacitated and possibly dead.
A situation where PCs and monsters interact, with time and movement measured in detail.
The order in which actions are resolved during an encounter.
A series of connected encounters; may be one session or a larger scenario.
A sequence of adventures, often involving the same characters.
A monster-filled underground complex containing monsters, treasure, and secrets.
A floor or depth of a dungeon; deeper levels are more dangerous.
A major structure such as a castle or tower that can attract followers.
Territory under a character's sovereign control.
A larger political entity formed from one or more domains.

general.rule: ACKS primarily uses d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, and d20.
d20 is used for attack throws and saving throws.
d10 is numbered 0-9; a roll of 0 counts as 10.
Two differently designated d10s can be rolled as percentile dice (d100). Declare tens and ones before rolling. 00 counts as 100.
d4 is effectively flipped rather than rolled; the upright number is the result.
Multiple dice are written as XdY, such as 2d6.

die_notation_table.entry: Roll two different d10s; one is tens, one is ones; 00 = 100.

rolling_dice.definition: A roll is used to determine which of several possible outcomes occurs.

procedure.step: Roll the appropriate die for the situation.
Apply the total as required by the situation.

notes.note: Some rolls produce absolute results, such as damage dealt.
Some rolls are compared to other rolls, such as initiative.
Some rolls are compared to tables.

throws.definition: A throw is a roll made when an action may succeed or fail.

procedure.step: Throw the appropriate die for the action.
Compare the total to the target value, usually written as a value such as 12+.
If the total equals or exceeds the target value, the outcome is favorable; otherwise it is unfavorable.

target_value_rule.rule: Throw target values are usually based on class and level.
Bonuses can be recorded as reductions to the target value instead of additions to the die roll.
Penalties can be recorded as increases to the target value instead of subtractions from the die roll.

die_selection_guidelines.rule: Use when outcomes are strongly influenced by both skill and fortune. Typical target values are 10-20. Modifiers have significant but not overwhelming impact.
Use when skill or innate ability matters strongly and randomness is lower. Used for surprise, initiative, and many damage rolls. Modifiers matter greatly because the range is small.
Use when many outcomes are possible but middle results should be most common. Produces a bell curve centered on 6-8. Used for reaction rolls and morale rolls.

standard_procedure.step: Start with a fresh character sheet.
Roll 3d6 in order for ability scores and record both scores and their bonuses or penalties.
Choose a class that fits the character's ability scores. Check prime requisites and minimum requirements. Record class special abilities.
Record 0 XP and optionally record the XP needed for 2nd level.

Roll hit points using the class Hit Die and add Constitution modifier. A Constitution penalty cannot reduce any Hit Die roll below 1. At Judge discretion, 1st-level characters may begin with maximum hp.
Record attack throws and saving throws for the class. Apply Strength to melee attacks and Dexterity to missile attacks.
Choose starting proficiencies. Apply all proficiency-based modifiers. If the character is a mage or elven spellsword, roll starting spells as described in the Spells chapter.

Roll starting wealth as 3d6 x 10 gp. Purchase equipment. Record remaining money. Obey class weapon and armor restrictions. Record AC including Dexterity modifier. Record weapon damage including Strength modifier. Calculate encumbrance.

procedure.step: Select one primary and two backups.
Give the remaining two to the Judge as NPCs.
If the primary and both backups die, repeat the procedure with five new characters.

generation.standard_method: Roll 3d6 for each ability in order.
generation.optional_method: The Judge may allow six scores to be rolled and assigned to abilities in any order.

effects.effect: Apply modifier to melee attack throws.
Apply modifier to melee damage rolls.
A Strength penalty cannot reduce damage from a successful attack below 1, unless the target is otherwise invulnerable to the attack.
Add Intelligence bonus to starting number of proficiencies.
Add Intelligence bonus to the number of languages the character can learn to read and write.
Mages, elven nightblades, and elven spellswords increase the number of spells of each level in their repertoire by their Intelligence bonus.

language_rules.rule: All characters begin knowing their native language.
Most humans also speak a common human language.
Demi-humans normally begin with their racial language, Common (or local equivalent), and certain other race-based languages.
A character with an Intelligence penalty knows only the native language and cannot read more than a word or two.
Characters with Intelligence 9-12 are literate in languages they can speak.
Characters with an Intelligence bonus may begin with additional languages equal to the bonus.
A player may leave one or more bonus language slots unassigned for later selection during play.
Possible languages include demi-human languages, beastman dialects, and Judge-approved ancient or exotic tongues.

effects.effect: Apply modifier to all saving throws, regardless of cause.
Apply modifier to missile attack throws.
Apply modifier to each Hit Die rolled.
A Constitution penalty cannot reduce any Hit Die roll below 1.
Maximum henchmen = 4 + Charisma modifier, producing a range of 1 to 7.
Average henchman morale is 0, modified by the character's Charisma bonus or penalty.

selection_rules.rule: A character must have at least 9 in each prime requisite to choose a class.
Some classes also have additional minimum ability requirements; these must be met.

xp_adjustment_rule.rule: If a class has two prime requisites, use the lower of the two scores to determine the XP adjustment.

ability_trade_rule.rule: After choosing a class, the player may raise the class's prime requisite ability or abilities by sacrificing other ability points.
Two points from another ability raise a prime requisite by one point.
This can be done more than once.
No ability can be reduced below 9.
No ability can be lowered if it is also a prime requisite for the class, even if above the minimum requirement.

rules.rule: Hit points measure survivability in combat.
At 0 or fewer hp, a character or other being is incapacitated and possibly dead.
Hit points are not a direct measure of physical injury only; they abstract fighting skill, stamina, luck, and divine favor.
Each class uses a different Hit Die.
One Hit Die is rolled at 1st level, and additional dice are rolled and added at later levels unless otherwise noted.
Optional rule: the Judge may allow 1st-level hp to be treated as the maximum result of the class Hit Die.

alignment_option.name: Lawful
alignment_option.definition: Supports civilization against those who would destroy it.

alignment_option.name: Neutral
alignment_option.definition: Generally pursues personal ends and does not strongly commit to Law or Chaos.

alignment_option.name: Chaotic
alignment_option.definition: Actively seeks to destroy civil society.

alignment.mechanical_note: These sections provide allegiance definitions; no direct mechanical modifiers are given in the provided text.

rules.rule: Characters usually form parties to survive dangerous adventures.
Parties may hire NPCs such as henchmen or mercenaries when extra manpower is needed.
If there are few players, the Judge may allow one player to run multiple characters.
Characters controlled by the same player may not give each other special treatment, such as trading or gifting wealth or magic items, unless the Judge allows it.
